source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nursing action is an example of client advocacy?
options: Giving information for an informed decision
questions.rationale: As an advocate, the nurse protects the client's human and legal rights and gives the information the client needs to make an informed decision. Obtaining consent is the provider's responsibility.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q401 (PDF p. 571)
questions.quote: The nurse advocates for the client by providing information needed so that the client can make an informed decision.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which task can the nurse safely delegate to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Delegation keeps accountability with the nurse. Nursing attendants are trained for noninvasive tasks such as delivering water, emptying urine bags, and taking vital signs of stable clients.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q403 (PDF p. 576)
questions.quote: Delegation is the transfer of responsibility for the performance of an activity or task while retaining accountability for the outcome.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which activity is SAFE to assign to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Delegated work must match the person's expertise. Collecting specimens and taking frequent oral temperatures carry little foreseeable risk. Assessment is not delegated.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q460 (PDF p. 642)
questions.quote: Work that is delegated to others must be consistent with the individual’s level of expertise and licensure, if any.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should the nurse tell a nursing attendant to do for a client with acute glomerulonephritis?
questions.rationale: Acute glomerulonephritis causes fluid excess and fatigue. Care includes fluid restriction, weight and I&O monitoring, and rest. Protein is limited.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q556 (PDF p. 757)
questions.quote: Interventions include fluid restriction, as well as monitoring weight and intake and output.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which guideline belongs in a policy on telephone and verbal orders?
options: Only the head nurse may receive them
questions.rationale: To avoid misunderstanding, the nurse clarifies any question with the prescriber and repeats the order back.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q410 (PDF p. 585)
questions.quote: the nurse would always clarify a telephone or verbal prescription with the health care provider (HCP) if he or she had any questions

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse finds an error in her handwritten chart entry. What should she do?
options: Draw one line and initial it
questions.rationale: A single line is drawn through the error and initialed so it stays readable. Errors are never erased, and correction fluid or markers are never used on a legal record.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q513 (PDF p. 708)
questions.quote: To correct a written error documented in a medical record, the nurse draws one line through the incorrect information and then initials the error.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A family friend calls the home health nurse offering to help a newborn's family. What is the BEST action?
options: Ask the friend to call the family
Invite the friend to the teaching
questions.rationale: The nurse gives no information about a client's care to anyone not directly involved in that care. Inviting the friend to teaching would violate the family's privacy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q420 (PDF p. 597)
questions.quote: The nurse must uphold the client’s rights and does not give any information regarding a client’s care needs to anyone who is not directly involved in the client’s care.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse gives a client's medical information to someone wrongly assumed to be family. Which rights were violated?
questions.rationale: Discussing a client's condition without permission violates the client's rights to privacy and confidentiality and puts the nurse in legal jeopardy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q449 (PDF p. 629)
questions.quote: Discussing a client’s condition without client permission violates a client’s rights to privacy and confidentiality

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which situation is an example of assault?
questions.rationale: Assault puts a person in fear of a harmful act. Battery is touching without permission, false imprisonment is unlawful restraint, and libel is a written falsehood.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q452 (PDF p. 632)
questions.quote: An assault occurs when a person puts another person in fear of a harmful or offensive act.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: After colon resection, a client with an NG tube is served solid food and asks for the doctor to be called. The nurse insists he eat, and he later needs more surgery. Which describes this?
questions.rationale: Negligence requires a duty, a breach of duty, injury caused by the breach, and damages. All four elements are present.
explanations: Correct: all four elements are present.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q454 (PDF p. 634)
questions.quote: For negligence to be proved, there must be a duty, and then a breach of duty; the breach of duty must cause the injury, and damages or injury must be experienced.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client asks how to become an organ donor. What should the nurse tell him?
questions.rationale: Anyone 18 years or older may donate by written consent without the family's permission or presence. This matches the Philippine Organ Donation Act (RA 7170).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q457 (PDF p. 638)
questions.quote: any person who is 18 years of age or older may become an organ donor by written consent without the permission or presence of the family.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Who is responsible for explaining a procedure and obtaining informed consent?
questions.rationale: Informed consent rests on full disclosure of risks, benefits, alternatives, and the consequences of refusal. The provider doing the procedure gives that information; the nurse may witness the signature.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q464 (PDF p. 646)
questions.quote: The primary health care provider (HCP) is responsible for conveying information and obtaining the informed consent.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: After the doctor explains a colonoscopy, the nurse finds the client cannot write. What is BEST?
options: Have two witnesses as he signs an X
questions.rationale: A client who cannot write may sign with an X in front of two witnesses. The nurse witnesses the signature, not whether the client was informed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q506 (PDF p. 701)
questions.quote: Clients who cannot write may sign an informed consent with an X in the presence of two witnesses.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An adult with severe dementia is scheduled for gallbladder surgery. What should the nurse do FIRST about consent?
questions.rationale: A mentally impaired client cannot give consent. Verifying the legal guardian avoids improperly signed documents and directs the surgeon to the right person.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q549 (PDF p. 750)
questions.quote: A mentally impaired client is not competent to sign an informed consent, so the nurse should first verify the identity of the client’s legal guardian.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A home care client says she does not want CPR. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: A client may refuse resuscitation. A written DNR order from the provider is needed so that her wishes are followed.
explanations: Correct: a DNR order is needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q481 (PDF p. 670)
questions.quote: a written “do not resuscitate” (DNR) prescription from the HCP is needed to ensure that the client’s wishes are followed.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client wants to leave the hospital before the doctor discharges him. What should the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: Informing the supervisor helps the nurse manage the situation safely and completely, including having the client sign a release (discharge against advice) form.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q581 (PDF p. 786)
questions.quote: The nurse notifies the nursing supervisor of the client’s plan to leave without the primary PHCP’s approval to ensure client safety

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A post-op client gets no pain relief from opioids only when one coworker is assigned. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Before acting on a suspicion, the nurse needs more data, which the record provides. Policies and drug laws then guide reporting.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q446 (PDF p. 626)
questions.quote: the nurse needs more data than just suspicion. This can be obtained by reviewing the client’s record.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client dies of gunshot wounds. Which action properly preserves evidence?
options: Bag the hands in paper bags
questions.rationale: Paper bags on the hands and feet protect trace evidence. Items go in paper bags, clothing is cut around holes, and evidence is not released to the family.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q497 (PDF p. 690)
questions.quote: placing paper bags on the hands and feet and possibly over the head of a deceased person (protects trace evidence and residue)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A client with stab wounds arrives in the ER. Which action BREAKS the rules for handling evidence?
options: Giving his wallet to the family
questions.rationale: Potential evidence is never released to the family. A chain of custody log tracks it, access is limited, and clothing is removed carefully.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q597 (PDF p. 805)
questions.quote: Potential evidence is never released to the family to take home.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which action shows a situational leadership style?
options: Asking for input on a problem
questions.rationale: Situational leaders change style with events, such as quickly delegating during an emergency. Laissez-faire leaders give up leadership; democratic leaders invite input.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q444 (PDF p. 624)
questions.quote: This type of leadership style is used in emergency situations when the nurse manager needs to quickly delegate activities

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which manager behavior shows an autocratic style?
questions.rationale: Autocratic leaders are task oriented and directive and decide without staff input.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q450 (PDF p. 630)
questions.quote: Decisions are made without input from the staff.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which leadership style lets staff give input to decisions and best empowers them?
questions.rationale: Democratic leadership lets nurses take part in decisions and grow professionally.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q487 (PDF p. 678)
questions.quote: this style of leadership allows nurses to provide input regarding the decision-making process and an opportunity to grow professionally.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which describes participative leadership?
questions.rationale: Participative leadership sits between authoritarian and democratic. The manager presents an analysis and proposals, invites comments, then makes the final decision.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q476 (PDF p. 661)
questions.quote: In participative leadership, the manager presents an analysis of problems and proposals for actions to team members, inviting critique and comments.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which situation shows primary nursing?
options: The RN gives all care to her client
An RN leads a mixed team
Each staff does one task for all
questions.rationale: Primary nursing keeps the nurse at the bedside, giving goal-directed, individualized care. Team nursing is led by an RN; functional nursing assigns tasks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q489 (PDF p. 680)
questions.quote: In primary nursing, option 1, concern is with keeping the nurse at the bedside actively involved in care

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The charge nurse has aides bathe clients, others pass water, and one RN give all medicines. Which model is this?
questions.rationale: Functional nursing is an assembly-line approach in which major tasks are assigned to individual staff members.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q501 (PDF p. 694)
questions.quote: The functional model of care involves an assembly line approach to client care, with major tasks being delegated by the charge nurse to individual staff members.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which describes team nursing?
options: An RN leads a team giving direct care
questions.rationale: In team nursing, an RN leads a team that gives direct care to a group of clients under the RN's supervision.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q562 (PDF p. 764)
questions.quote: The team members provide direct client care to groups of clients under the direct supervision of the RN team leader.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement describes case management?
options: It coordinates care and limits costs
The case manager gives all bedside care
It is done by one discipline
questions.rationale: Case management coordinates services for clients and families while keeping quality high and costs low. Case managers usually do not give direct care and work with other disciplines.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q541 (PDF p. 739)
questions.quote: Case management is a care management approach that coordinates health care services to clients and their families while maintaining quality of care and minimizing health care costs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which function belongs to the unit nurse manager?
questions.rationale: The middle manager recruits and hires staff, holds staff meetings, helps staff meet unit goals, and monitors standards of practice.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q561 (PDF p. 763)
questions.quote: Responsibilities of the nurse manager (middle manager) include recruiting new employees (interviewing and hiring), conducting regular staff meetings

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A staff nurse cannot meet client needs on time or prioritize care. What should the charge nurse do?
options: Ask others to do her work
Support her and find the cause
questions.rationale: Supporting the nurse and identifying the underlying cause helps reduce the problem. The other options are punitive or shift the burden to others.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q484 (PDF p. 675)
questions.quote: Option 3 empowers the charge nurse to assist the staff nurse while trying to identify and reduce the behaviors that make it difficult for the staff nurse to function.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A preceptor watches a new nurse manage her time. Which action needs correcting?
questions.rationale: Documentation is done continuously during the day. Planning breaks, gathering supplies, and combining tasks are good time management.
explanations: Correct answer: chart as you go.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q485 (PDF p. 676)
questions.quote: The nurse should document task completion continuously throughout the day.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which item in the home puts a client recovering from hip surgery at risk for injury?
questions.rationale: Home injuries often come from tripping on doormats, small rugs, or clutter. Night-lights and raised seats with armrests reduce hazards.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q466 (PDF p. 649)
questions.quote: Injuries in the home frequently result from tripping over or coming into contact with common household objects such as a doormat, small rugs on the floor or stairs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which procedure requires surgical asepsis?
questions.rationale: Sterile technique is used for applying sterile dressings, inserting IV or urinary catheters, and tracheal suctioning. Clean technique is used for removing dressings and giving oral medicines.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q545 (PDF p. 746)
questions.quote: Some examples of procedures in which surgical asepsis is necessary include reapplying sterile dressings, inserting an IV or urinary catheter

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: During a disaster, which victim needs IMMEDIATE (red tag) care?
questions.rationale: Arterial bleeding from the neck is life-threatening and is tagged red. Green (minimal) victims can wait.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q598 (PDF p. 806)
questions.quote: The client with bright red (arterial) bleeding from a neck wound is in “immediate” need of treatment to save the client’s life.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Beds are needed for disaster victims. Which client should STAY in the hospital?
questions.rationale: Ongoing ventricular dysrhythmias need continued treatment because they can be fatal. Stable conditions can be managed at home with referrals.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q599 (PDF p. 807)
questions.quote: The client with ongoing ventricular dysrhythmias requires ongoing medical evaluation and treatment because of potentially lethal complications of the problem.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A client with suspected smallpox arrives in the ER. What should the plan include FIRST?
questions.rationale: With a communicable disease such as smallpox, the client is isolated immediately and staff put on protective equipment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q491 (PDF p. 682)
questions.quote: the client would be isolated immediately and the staff would immediately don protective equipment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which action is correct for a client exposed to anthrax?
questions.rationale: Decontamination includes having the client remove contaminated clothing, handling it minimally, and storing it in a labeled paper bag.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q540 (PDF p. 738)
questions.quote: Decontamination and exposure management of the client suspected of anthrax exposure include instructing the client to remove contaminated clothing
